title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:
As an AP Assistant in Milton Keynes, you'll handle the day-to-day processing of invoices and payments, ensuring the smooth operation of the accounts payable function. This role is key to maintaining accurate financial records and supporting the wider finance team within the business services industry.

Client Details

This company operates within the business services industry and is based in Milton Keynes.

Description
- Process high volumes of supplier invoices accurately and efficiently within agreed service levels.
- Manage the end-to-end Purchase-to-Pay (P2 P) process, including invoice coding, PO matching and approval workflows.
- Support weekly and monthly payment runs, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time.
- Reconcile supplier statements, investigate discrepancies and resolve outstanding queries promptly.
- Respond to supplier and internal stakeholder queries, maintaining excellent customer service standards.
- Maintain accurate vendor records and ensure financial data is complete, accurate and up to date.
- Assist with month-end activities, including reconciliations, accruals and reporting requirements.
- Identify process improvements and support the continuous development of Accounts Payable procedures.
- Ensure compliance with company policies, financial controls and audit requirements.
- Provide support to the wider finance team and assist with ad hoc projects as required.

Profile

A successful AP Assistant should have:
- Previous experience within Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger or a transactional finance environment.
- Good understanding of Accounts Payable processes, including invoice processing, reconciliations and supplier payments.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to process high volumes of transactions accurately.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to prioritise workload to meet deadlines.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and experience using finance or ERP systems.
- Strong communication skills with the confidence to liaise with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- A proactive and solutions-focused approach to resolving queries and improving processes.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative finance team.
- Commitment to maintaining accurate records and operating within established financial controls.
- A positive attitude with a willingness to learn and support the wider finance function.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £28,000 to £33,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position based in Milton Keynes.
- 4 days in office.
- Additional benefits to be confirmed.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller

Location: Milton Keynes - Hybrid

This role follows a non-negotiable 3-day hybrid working pattern. Candidates must live within a reasonable commuting distance of our Milton Keynes office.

About the job:

We're looking for a Credit Controller to join our Finance team at Ingram Micro UK. As the business continues to evolve, we're looking for someone with Credit Control experience who can confidently manage customer accounts, build strong stakeholder relationships and support cash collection performance.

You'll take ownership of a portfolio of sales-driven and account-managed customers, working closely with Sales, Finance and Credit Risk teams to resolve issues, minimise risk and support the financial performance of the business.

Whilst the ideal candidate will bring strong Credit Control experience, we're also keen to hear from those earlier in their Credit Control career who are looking to develop their skills within a supportive, global business. If you're looking for an opportunity to grow, take ownership and build a long-term career in Credit Control, we'd love to hear from you.

Core responsibilities:
- Managing the timely collection of customer debt across a portfolio of key accounts
- Building strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders to resolve queries and drive payment performance
- Reviewing held orders and making informed decisions to support order release and minimise risk
- Investigating and resolving escalated customer queries and complaints
- Working closely with Sales, Finance, Credit Risk and our third-party collections provider to manage complex accounts
- Producing debtor reporting, cash forecasts and other working capital reports as required
- Supporting continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance processes and ways of working

To set you up for success, we are looking for the following skills and experience:
- Experience in a Credit Control role is essential. We welcome applicants at all levels of experience, including those early in their Credit Control career, but candidates must have worked specifically in Credit Control rather than solely in a broader finance position.
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders
- Good analytical skills and confidence interpreting financial information
- Confident using Excel, including Pivot Tables and VLOOKUPs
- A proactive approach, with the ability to manage priorities and take ownership of issues through to resolution

What we offer:
- AXA Health Insurance and Dental Plan options available for you and your family through a salary sacrifice scheme
- Rising holiday allowance at Year 2 and Year 5
- Birthday day off
- Employee Referral Bonus - help us grow our team and get rewarded for introducing great talent
- Employee discounts and wellness perks
- Modern offices with breakout spaces, free tea and coffee, and a private wellness room
- Development opportunities with clear career progression and training

We Are Ingram Micro Group

Ingram Micro is a leading technology company for the global information technology ecosystem. With the ability to reach nearly 90% of the global population, we play a vital role in the worldwide IT sales channel, bringing products and services from technology manufacturers and cloud providers to business-to-business technology experts. Through Ingram Micro Xvantage, our AI-powered digital platform, we offer what we believe to be the industry's first business-to- consumer-like experience. We also provide a broad range of technology services, including financing, specialized marketing, and lifecycle management, as well as technical pre- and post- sales professional support.

If this sounds like the opportunity for you then please apply by sending a copy of your most recent CV.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team at Purbeck Health Centre. This is an important front-line role where you will help patients access the right care while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Friendly, approachable and professional Reliable, organised and able to manage competing priorities Confident communicating with patients and colleagues Comfortable using computers and learning new systems Able to work independently and as part of a team Committed to providing excellent patient service Previous experience in a GP practice or healthcare setting would be helpful, but it is not essential. Full training will be provided, and you will be supported by an experienced team who take pride in delivering excellent care and service to our patients. If you are looking for a rewarding and varied role where you can make a real difference to patients every day, we would love to hear from you. What you will be doing Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries Welcoming patients at the reception desk Booking and managing appointments Completing a variety of administrative tasks Working closely with our clinical and administrative teams Handling confidential information professionally The role is busy and varied, so you will need excellent communication and organisational skills, good attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. Job Description Job title: Receptionist/Administrator Location: Purbeck Health Centre, Milton Keynes Hours: Working pattern to be agreed Reports to: Reception Lead/Practice Manager The Receptionist/Administrator will be one of the first points of contact for patients and visitors. The postholder will provide a professional and welcoming reception service, manage telephone calls and patient enquiries, and complete a range of computer-based administrative duties. The role is essential to supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and ensuring patients receive a helpful, efficient and respectful service. Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, caring and professional manner. Check patients in for appointments and assist with general enquiries. Support the smooth flow of patients through the practice. Communicate with clinicians and other team members when required. Keep the reception area calm, tidy and organised. Respect patients privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and courteously. Book, amend and cancel appointments accurately using SystmOne. Respond to general enquiries and direct patients to the appropriate service or member of staff. Follow practice procedures when receiving urgent or emergency calls and escalate concerns immediately where required. Take clear and accurate messages and pass them to the appropriate clinician or administrator promptly. Communicate sensitively with patients who may be worried, distressed or frustrated. Update patient contact details, appointment information and records accurately. Process online appointment requests, messages and administrative queries. Maintain accurate patient records, tasks and worklists on SystmOne. Monitor emails, call queues and other practice communication systems. Support the smooth running of the days appointments and reception services. Complete general administrative duties, including printing letters, preparing lists and entering data. Follow practice procedures for filing, communication and information sharing. Work closely with reception colleagues to maintain appropriate cover for the front desk and telephone lines. Communicate clearly and professionally with clinicians, administrators and management. Provide additional cover during colleagues annual leave or sickness where required. Attend team meetings, training sessions and practice updates. Contribute ideas that could improve patient services or working processes. Promote a positive, respectful and supportive working environment. Follow all practice policies and procedures, including those relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and data protection. Maintain a professional, respectful and positive approach. Report incidents, risks or concerns promptly to the Reception Lead or Practice Manager. Complete all required mandatory training. Keep knowledge of practice systems, policies and procedures up to date. Work within the responsibilities and boundaries of the role. Excellent communication and telephone skills. A friendly, polite and approachable manner. Confidence using computers and learning new systems. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. Ability to remain calm and professional in a busy environment. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. A reliable, flexible and supportive approach to teamwork. Understanding of the importance of patient confidentiality. Commitment to providing a high standard of patient service. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare setting or customer-facing role. Experience using SystmOne or another clinical record system. The postholder must promote equality, diversity and inclusion and treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, fairness and respect. The postholder must take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their work. Any hazards, incidents or concerns must be reported promptly in accordance with practice procedures. All patient, staff and practice information must be treated as confidential. The postholder must follow UK GDPR, data protection requirements, NHS information governance standards and practice policies. The postholder will be expected to: Uphold the values and reputation of Purbeck Health Centre. Follow all practice policies, procedures and applicable NHS requirements. Take responsibility for their own learning, training and professional development. Contribute to a positive, supportive and inclusive workplace. Carry out other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. This job description provides an overview of the role and is not exhaustive. Duties may change as the needs of the practice develop, following appropriate discussion with the postholder and their line manager.
